sections.title: Tree and flowers
sections.text: Prunus padus, bird cherry, is a tree or large shrub often reaching 14–15 m. Its leaves are about 5–10 cm long. Fragrant white flowers grow in long hanging racemes.

sections.title: Fruit and toxicity
sections.text: The black drupes are about 6–8 mm across and very bitter; the pulp is used in some preserves and drinks. Seeds and bark contain cyanogenic glycosides, and the plant can poison grazing animals.
